purpose: Teach: 理系/支局/新卒/勘弁/不適切/言い分/脱却/未定

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、お前は、本気で、絶対、理系、絶対、出身、絶対、誇りに思え、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Ren — I need you to be genuinely proud of your science background. I'm serious about this.
lines.style: Warm, direct authority. Opens with the name as gentle anchor. Slight pause after the dash. Steady eye contact through the request. Not harsh—mentoring. A 'because I believe in you' tone underneath.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。海外、本気で、絶対、支局、絶対、研究者、絶対、と、絶対、共同、絶対、しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm genuinely grateful for the opportunity to collaborate with overseas researchers at the branch office.
lines.style: Earnest and steady. No performative formality, but careful with words. Slight breath before 'grateful'—the emotion is real, not rehearsed. Measured pace. Looking at him directly.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、卒業後、本気で、絶対、新卒、絶対、として、絶対、就活、絶対、頑張れ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: After you graduate, I want you to give the job search your full effort. I'm counting on you.
lines.style: Firm but not cold. The 'after you graduate' lands with gentle weight—acknowledgment of a milestone. 'Full effort' carries conviction. The closing feels personal, not ceremonial. Direct and calm.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: すみません、お時間遅刻、本気で、絶対、勘弁、絶対、してくださいませ、本気で、感謝
lines.en: I apologize for running late. Thank you for your patience and understanding.
lines.style: Quick, quiet apology—no self-flagellation. A slight dip in the voice on 'apologize,' then recovery. Respectful but not groveling. Tight, efficient delivery. Genuine, not formulaic.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、研究、本気で、絶対、不適切、絶対、な、絶対、引用、絶対、避けろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Ren — be careful with your citations. Avoid any shortcuts in your research. This matters.
lines.style: Shift to slightly firmer. Not angry, but the concern is clear. 'Avoid any shortcuts' lands with quiet seriousness. Slight lean forward in the voice. Protective tone—he's warning, not punishing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。教授の、本気で、絶対、言い分、絶対、よく、絶対、伺っております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm listening carefully to what you're saying about the methodology. I understand.
lines.style: Attentive, nodding in the voice. No rushing. 'Listening carefully' gets soft emphasis—he wants Hiroshi to know he's engaged, not just compliant. Slight pause before 'understand' to let it land.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、古い研究法、本気で、絶対、脱却、絶対、しろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Ren — it's time to move past those old methods. You're ready for something better.
lines.style: Encouraging shift. The 'it's time' carries momentum, not pressure. 'Something better' is said with quiet confidence in him. Slight warmth returns. Believe-in-you energy, not disappointment.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。学位授与日、本気で、絶対、未定、絶対、で、絶対、お待ちしております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. We're still finalizing the details on the degree conferral date, but I'm ready whenever it happens.
lines.style: Calm, grounded close. Slight smile in the voice—acceptance of uncertainty. 'Whenever it happens' is patient, not anxious. The tone is: I'm prepared, moving forward. Warm but professional ending.
